title: Praising God
note: A poet praises his own god or the god suited to his subject. He says this is the second: the book treats three goals, each tied to one of the three first gods, so the praise is addressed to all three in common.

couplets.plain: As all letters begin with A, the world begins with the First Lord.
couplets.pm: All letters have A as their first, and the world likewise has the First Lord. A leads because it arises by nature as bare sound, not by change. The Lord leads because he knows everything by nature, not by learning. “All letters” includes Sanskrit, and “world” means living beings. The seen world is named to show that the unseen god exists.

links.quote: the world begins with the First Lord
links.reason: Names the First Lord as the source of the world, as A stands first among all letters.

couplets.plain: What use is learning to those who won’t worship the good feet of the one whose knowledge is pure?
couplets.pm: What use is the learning of someone who has read every book, if they don’t worship the good feet of the one with true knowledge? None. The feet are good because they cure the disease of birth. The use of scriptural knowledge is to worship his feet and so end birth.

links.quote: worship the good feet
the one whose knowledge is pure
links.reason: Calls him the one whose knowledge is pure, which is why a student’s learning should bow to him.

links.quote: the good feet
links.reason: Worship at the feet stands for all devotion, the only real return on learning.

couplets.plain: Those who reach the noble feet of the one who walked on the flower will live long on the earth.
couplets.pm: Those who reach the glorious feet of the one who goes upon the flower live forever in the world of release, above all worlds. The flower is the heart’s lotus: he hurries there, in the form they imagine, for those who think of him with love. To reach his feet is to think of him without a break. Some give this to another god because of the title “walker on flowers”.
couplets.note: The words say long life “on the earth”. He takes நிலமிசை as above all worlds, the world of release, and the flower as the heart.

links.quote: will live long on the earth
links.reason: Promises long life on earth to those who reach the feet of the one who walked on the flower.

links.quote: the noble feet
links.reason: The feet of the one who walked on the flower are the place to reach.

couplets.plain: Those who reach the feet of the one who wants nothing and rejects nothing will have no suffering, ever.
couplets.pm: Those who reach the feet of the one who neither longs for nor hates anything have no suffering of birth at any time. That suffering is of three kinds: from yourself, from other beings and from the gods. Those who reach his feet are also free of longing and hatred, so the three sufferings, which come from those two, don’t arise.

links.quote: will have no suffering, ever
links.reason: Says those who reach his feet will never suffer.

links.quote: the one who wants nothing and rejects nothing
links.reason: Praises him as one who wants nothing and rejects nothing.

links.quote: reach the feet
links.reason: Reaching the feet is what puts people beyond suffering.

couplets.plain: The two kinds of deeds, which go with darkness, do not touch those devoted to the true praise of the Lord.
couplets.pm: Neither of the two deeds, good and bad, which come of delusion, comes to those who always speak the true praise of the Lord. Delusion is called darkness because no one can say what it is. Good deeds count too, because they also cause birth. The ignorant praise others who lack the Lord’s qualities, and that praise is empty. Only praise of him, who has them all, is true.

links.quote: devoted to the true praise of the Lord
links.reason: Devotion to the Lord’s true praise is what keeps both kinds of deeds away.

links.quote: The two kinds of deeds, which go with darkness
links.reason: Counts both kinds of deeds as bound up with darkness, and being free of them as the gain.

couplets.plain: Those who stay on the true path of the one who quenched the five senses will live long.
couplets.pm: The one who cut off the five desires that work through the senses of body, mouth, eyes, nose and ears taught a true path of conduct. Those who never stray from it live for all time, free of birth and unchanging. There are five desires because there are five sense objects. Couplets 3 to 6 say that those who think of the Lord, praise him and keep to his path gain release.

links.quote: stay on the true path
links.reason: Long life goes to those who stay on the true path of the one who quenched the senses.

links.quote: quenched the five senses
links.reason: The one they follow is praised for quenching the five senses, the pattern for his followers.

couplets.plain: Unless you reach the feet of the one who has no equal, the sorrow in your mind is hard to remove.
couplets.pm: Only those who reach the feet of the one without equal in any way can remove the sorrows of the mind. “Hard” here means it can’t be done. Those who don’t reach his feet can’t end the desire, anger and delusion that cause birth, so they are born and die and sink in the suffering these bring.

links.quote: the sorrow in your mind is hard to remove
links.reason: Makes reaching his feet the way to lift sorrow from the mind.

links.quote: the one who has no equal
links.reason: Calls him the one who has no equal, which is why nothing else lifts the sorrow.

links.quote: reach the feet
links.reason: Names his feet as the one place where sorrow of the mind can be lifted.

couplets.plain: Unless you reach the feet of the sage who is a sea of righteousness, the other seas are hard to swim.
couplets.pm: Only those who reach the raft of the feet of the sage who is a sea of righteousness can swim the other seas, which are wealth and pleasure. All kinds of righteousness make up his form, so he is called a sea of it. Those who don’t reach that raft see no shore and sink. Some read the sea as a wheel of righteousness.
couplets.note: பிறவாழி can also be taken as the sea of births, as in K10. He takes it as “other seas”, meaning wealth and pleasure.

links.quote: reach the feet of the sage
links.reason: Only by reaching the sage’s feet can anyone swim the other seas.

links.quote: the other seas are hard to swim
links.reason: Uses seas twice: the sage is a sea of righteousness, and what lies before everyone else are seas to be swum.

links.quote: the feet of the sage
links.reason: The feet are what a swimmer in those seas must reach.

couplets.plain: A head that won’t bow at the feet of the one with eight qualities is as useless as a sense that senses nothing.
couplets.pm: Heads that don’t bow to the feet of the one with eight qualities are as useless as senses that can’t take in their objects. The Saiva scriptures list the eight: independence, a pure body, natural understanding, knowing all, natural freedom from bonds, great compassion, endless power and boundless joy. Tongues that don’t praise him are just as useless.

links.quote: A head that won’t bow
the feet of the one with eight qualities

couplets.plain: Those who reach the Lord’s feet swim the great sea of births. Those who do not reach them will not.
couplets.pm: Those who reach the raft of the Lord’s feet swim the great sea of birth. Those who don’t can’t swim and sink in it. Those who think only of his feet and not of the world’s ways have their births ended, and those who think otherwise don’t.

links.quote: Those who do not reach them will not
links.reason: Allows no other way across: those who do not reach the Lord’s feet will not swim the sea.

links.quote: swim the great sea of births
links.reason: Swimming the sea of births is the end of being born, the prize held out here.

links.quote: the great sea of births
links.reason: Birth after birth is one great sea that has to be swum.

links.quote: the Lord’s feet

ideaLinks.quote: What use is learning to those who won’t worship
ideaLinks.reason: All learning is useless unless it ends in worship.

ideaLinks.quote: do not touch those devoted to the true praise of the Lord
ideaLinks.reason: Devotion to the Lord’s true praise keeps both kinds of deeds from touching a person.

ideaLinks.quote: the sorrow in your mind is hard to remove
ideaLinks.reason: Reaching the feet of the one with no equal is what lifts sorrow from the mind.

ideaLinks.quote: Those who reach the Lord’s feet swim the great sea of births
ideaLinks.reason: Reaching the Lord’s feet is what lets a person swim the great sea of births.
